title: Friend List
story: You just joined a new social platform and want to manage your friend list. Tom added you, you added Lisa, but did Mike accept your request? You need to add friends, remove them, and check who's in your circle — all in order.
why: Vec with for-loops is the simplest way to manage ordered lists of items — friends are added in order, displayed in order, and searched in order.
analogy: A Vec friend list is like a sign-up sheet on a clipboard — names appear in the order they were written. You can scan down the list to find someone, cross a name out (remove), or add to the bottom (push).
expected_output:
Friend: Tom
Friend: Lisa
Friend: Aisha
Friend: Miguel
true
4
try_it: Write a `count_friends_starting_with` function that counts how many friends' names start with a given letter. Then build a `mutual_friends` function that takes two friend lists and returns a Vec of names that appear in both. What data structure helps make the mutual search faster?
tips: Use `for item in &vec` to read every element — the `&` borrows so you don't lose ownership
Linear scan with `.get(i)` and while works for searching — simple but effective for small lists
Keep a separate tracking Vec if you need iteration order — Map and Set don't preserve insertion order
common_mistakes: Writing `for friend in friends` without `&` — this moves each element out, breaking the Vec
Using `.contains()` on Vec — Vec doesn't have `.contains()`, only Set does; use a manual loop
Trying to modify a Vec while iterating with for — build a new Vec with filtered items instead
